minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 14, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:07 p.m., on June 14, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 9, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths (arrived at 5:57 p.m.)
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel and Police Chief Pursuant to Government Code
  54957(a) on Matters Posing a Threat to Public Services, Facilities and Operations;
  City of Mission Viejo; Police Coverage and Scoping.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  1  June 14, 2016
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m. Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Joey Likar, Jaren Kawai, and Tyler Yu: discussed their participation in an elective engineering
class at Newhart Middle School led by teacher and former engineer, Eric Gosselin. The Newhart
robotics teams recently won awards for their Remote Operate Vehicle (ROV) at technology
competitions at Cal State Long Beach and Capistrano Valley High School.

James Farris, M.V.: stated that the building department has failed homeowners to maintain, fix, or
upgrade houses within the city limits.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 7, 12, 13, and 16 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT: None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of May 10, 2016, as amended,
  and May 24, 2016, as presented.

City Council Minutes  2  June 14, 2016
 3.  General Municipal Election - November 8, 2016

  (1) Adopted Resolution 16-24 Calling for the Holding of a General Municipal Election to
  be Held on Tuesday, November 8, 2016, for the Election of Certain Officers as Required
  by the Provisions of the Laws of the State of California Relating to General Law Cities; (2)
  adopted Resolution 16-25 Requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Orange
  to Consolidate a General Municipal Election to be Held on November 8, 2016 with the
  Statewide General Election to be Held on the Same Date pursuant to § 10403 of the
  Elections Code; (3) adopted Resolution 16-26 Adopting Regulations for Candidates for
  Elective Officer Pertaining to Candidates Statements Submitted to the Voters at an Election
  to be Held on November 8, 2016; and (4) directed the City Clerk to schedule the adoption
  of the resolution citing the election results and administration of the oath to the newly
  elected Council Members on December 13, 2016, or as soon as possible thereafter.

4.  Check Register Dated May 13, 2016 in the Amount of $2,010,356.54

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated May 20, 2016 in the Amount of $510,620.18

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated May 27, 2016 in the Amount of $1,130,803.06

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  Adoption of FY 2016-17 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority

  Adopted CDFA Resolution 16-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Financing Authority for the 2016-17 Fiscal Year.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Budget – Fiscal Year 2016-17

  Adopted Housing Authority Resolution 16-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority (MVHA) for FY 2016-17.

10.  Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre – Year 2016 – Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 16-28 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt on
  Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City Council
  to Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for Hearing
  Protests; (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to Destroy Weeds
  in accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3) instructed the City
  Clerk to set the Public Hearing for August 23, 2016.
City Council Minutes  3  June 14, 2016
 11.  Purchase of Two Animal Services Vehicles

  Awarded a Purchase Agreement for two Animal Service Vehicles to Tuttle Click Ford in
  an amount not to exceed $158,180.00 on July 1, 2016.

13.  Contract Amendment - SiteOne Landscape Supply, LLC and Cancellation of Hydro-
  Scape Products, Inc. Contract

  (1) Approved Third Amendment with SiteOne Landscape Supply, LLC., increasing the
  contract by $188,300.00, for a total contract amount not to exceed $443,300.00; and (2)
  canceled the existing contract with Hydro-Scape Products, Inc.

15.  Contract Amendment - Tom Bistline Construction, Inc. Name Change

  (1) Approved the First Amendment to the Tom Bistline Construction Inc. agreement for
  the Annual Maintenance Program for the Repair and Reconstruction of Streets, Drainage
  Channels, Storm Drains, Slopes Emergency Response and Heavy Equipment to reflect the
  change of the company's name to WB Management, Inc. DBA Bistline Engineering; (2)
  cancel the Tom Bistline Construction Inc. associated license agreement for the use and
  storage of emergency response equipment on city parcel and issue new license agreement
  to WB Management, Inc. DBA Bistline Engineering.

17.  Los Alisos Boulevard Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Program (Project P)
  and Santa Margarita Parkway Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Program
  (Project P)

  (1) Approved Amendment No. 1 to Cooperative Agreement NO. C-2-1996 for the Los
  Alisos Boulevard Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Program (Project P); and (2)
  approved Amendment No. 1 to Cooperative Agreement NO. C-2-1994 for the Santa
  Margarita Parkway Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Program (Project P).

18.  Reissuance of the Variance to Municipal Code 97-169 for Casta del Sol Homeowners
  Association

  Authorized staff to reissue the variance to the Casta del Sol Homeowners Association for
  Municipal Code Firearm Ordinance 97-169.

19.  Reissuance of the Variance to Municipal Code 97-169 for Palmia Homeowners
  Association

  Authorized staff to reissue the variance to the Palmia Homeowners Association for
  Municipal Code Firearm Ordinance 97-169.

STAFF REPORTS

City Council Minutes  4  June 14, 2016
 26.  FY 2016-17 Law Enforcement Services Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1) approve the FY
  2016-17 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of Orange (A16-20) for
  an amount not to exceed $18,352,156; and (2) authorize the City Manager to approve
  reimbursements related to special enforcement services in an amount not to exceed $65,000
  for FY 2016-17.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Mayor Ury

28.  Report on Meeting with Capistrano Unified School District Superintendent Kirsten
  Vital and Trustee Gila Jones regarding the proposed CUSD Bond Measure

  City Manager Wilberg discussed the recent meeting with CUSD Superintendent Vital and
  Trustee Jones.

  The following expressed concern with the amount of money the school district is proposing
  for the bond measure and that the district can't identify where the money will be spent:
  Sharon Campbell, M.V. and Wayne Tate, M.V.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

7.  Mission Viejo Community Facilities District No 92-1 - Annual Special Tax for Fiscal
  Year 2016-17

  Council Member Sachs asked if any of the parcel owners have ever been delinquent with
  their payments.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas responded that Sports Authority made
  one late payment but otherwise, there have been no delinquencies.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to adopt Resolution 16-
  27 Establishing an Annual Special Tax for Fiscal Year 2016-17 for Community Facilities
  District No. 92-1 (Mission Viejo Freeway Center).
City Council Minutes  5  June 14, 2016
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

12.  Purchase Two Toyota Prius - Replacement Code Enforcement Vehicles

  Council Member Sachs noted that the recommended vehicles are primarily battery operated
  and the batteries have a stated lifetime. He said that new batteries cost anywhere from
  $3,000 to $6,000 and he expressed concern with the proposed lease payment of more than
  $400 per month.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to table
  this item and direct staff to look at other ways of finding vehicles that will suit the City's
  needs and can be leased or purchased at more appropriate rates.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT: None

14.  Eldorado Park Playground Renovations - (CIP 305)

  Council Member Schlicht reminded staff that she is interested in looking at age appropriate
  equipment for older kids.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that
  renovations for Eldorado park had been designed before her suggestion came up
  previously. He said that Recreation and Community Services may be working on
  equipment for older kids but he is not aware of any current plans.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to award a contract
  to JMJ Construction (A16-18) for Eldorado Park Playground Renovations in an amount
  not to exceed $563,191.50.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  6  June 14, 2016
 16.  2016-2017 School Crossing Guard Services

  Council Member Sachs asked questions relative to the total payments under the contract
  and the recommended pay increase for the crossing guards.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon responded to questions and said he could provide
  additional information after reviewing the original contract and prior amendments.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to table this item and
  direct staff to bring it back with clarification at the next City Council Meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

OLD BUSINESS

20.  Mission Viejo Animal Service Center Design Contract

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to award
  a contract to Gillis + Panichapan Architects Inc. and issue a Purchase Order on July 1, 2016
  in an amount not to exceed $48,185.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

21.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

22.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

City Council Minutes  7  June 14, 2016
 23.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

24.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

City Manager Wilberg highlighted two handouts that were distributed to the Council; a status
report on the Marguerite Aquatics Center renovation project and material that the Mayor requested
regarding the Capistrano Unified School District including a resolution on the establishment of
school facility standards.

25.  Adoption of the Revised FY 2016-17 City Operating and Capital Improvement
  Program Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to adopt Resolution 16-
  29 Adopting a Revised Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for FY 2016-17 and
  Appropriating Funds for FY 2016-17; (2) adopt Resolution 16-30 Amending the City's
  Salary Schedule and Establishing Salary Ranges for Authorized Job Classifications; and
  (3) adopt Resolution 16-31 Revising the City's Flexible Benefit Plan and Fixed Monthly
  City Contribution Schedule.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

27.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths acknowledged a member of the audience, Mary-Lee Robinson. He noted
that he works with Mary-Lee on the Oso Valley Greenbelt Association Board of Directors. Council
City Council Minutes  8  June 14, 2016
 Member Raths said she works very hard to keep the community looking beautiful and he thanked
her for all that she does.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs reported on his participation in the League of California Cities Employee
Relations Committee which deals with pensions. The committee members had the honor of
hearing CalPERS Chief Actuary, Alan Milligan, speak at the last meeting. Mr. Milligan talked
about the efforts to reduce and clarify the risks involved in the funding of the CalPERS System
and he recommended changes in the law, contribution rates, and actuarial tables. Council Member
Sachs said that reduction of risk will increase the amount of money that the City will have to pay
into the CalPERS pension fund in the future.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht thanked Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix for
a successful teen night and for creating opportunities for a segment of the population that has been
underserved. She explained that her passion for this developed when five teens were killed while
returning from Knott's Berry Farm a few years ago and she also knew a girl who died in a car
accident when she was a kid. Council Member Schlicht inquired about the distribution of the
PACE information letter for residents and asked that it be posted on the City's website. She also
thanked Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay for his response to her questions on the type of weed
killer that the City uses and she noted that she would hand in information from National
Geographic and Scientific American on the dangers of chemicals in weed killers. Council Member
Schlicht thanked City Manager Wilberg for his response to her questions on Olympic Day. She
said that she was concerned about messaging for a particular City Council candidate but she is sure
that it is just coincidence and she will add that information to the record as well. Council Member
Schlicht said that this is a very sad time for our nation after the terrorist massacre in Orlando,
Florida, and she reminded residents of the motto, "If you see something, say something." She said
that Americans cannot be grateful enough for first responders who have now basically become an
army in our nation. She asked for prayers and condolences for the family and friends of the victims
and in closing, Council Member Schlicht read a quote from George W. Bush: "We're too great a
nation to allow the evildoers to affect our soul."

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum announced that the City received a Golden Hub of Innovation
Award from the Association of California Cities-Orange County for its partnership with the Santa
Margarita Water District and the Lake Association. She and Mayor Ury were present at the awards
ceremony and it was truly a team acceptance with representatives of the other agencies on hand as
well. She reminded residents that the DAWG Walk, which benefits the City’s animal welfare
group, will be held on Saturday, June 18, 2016, beginning at 8:00 a.m. at the Village Green. Mayor
Pro Tem Bucknum congratulated Council Member Sachs on his election to the Republican Central
Committee and she also congratulated all of the high school graduates in the City. She noted that
the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce is celebrating its five-year anniversary and she is very
City Council Minutes  9  June 14, 2016
 proud that they are here and thriving five years later. She asked about the upcoming Olympic Day
event and Assistant City Manager Rattay clarified that there will be an Olympic send-off event
(for Olympic hopefuls) on Monday, June 20 at the Marguerite Aquatics Center pool and then, on
June 28, there will be an Olympic Day event at Florence Joyner park beginning at 1:00 p.m. Mayor
Pro Tem Bucknum invited residents to come out to one or both events.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury announced that his daughter is engaged to a young man who works for Northrop
Grumman. This past weekend he took his wife and sons to the Northrop facility in Palmdale for
Family Day and they were able to see the very impressive B2 Bomber while they were there. He
also discussed the City’s Golden Hub of Innovation award for the Advanced Water Purification
partnership project which was spearheaded by the Santa Margarita Water District. Mayor Ury
noted that the equipment is arriving and there will be a grand opening event in late July or early
August.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:09 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in solidarity with the victims and the people affected by the
massacre in Orlando, to Tuesday, June 28, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 28, 2016

City Council Minutes  10  June 14, 2016
